artifact_audits.first_material_issue_summary: Line 91 contains an off-by-one factorial error: claims (p-1)! ≡ (-1)^r r! · (p-r)! (mod p) when it should be (p-r-1)!, as the product (p-1)(p-2)...(p-r) contains r terms leaving (p-r-1)! remaining

The proof falsely claims ∠GBA = 90° because 'AB = AC makes ∠A = 90° in the isosceles triangle' - this is incorrect as AB = AC only implies the triangle is isosceles, not that it is an isosceles right triangle with ∠A = 90°.

The proof incorrectly claims there is at most one root 'by monotonicity' without verifying that f(t_0) < 0 is impossible, which would yield two distinct solutions.

The proof unjustifiably asserts that distinct pairs (a²,b²) and (c²,d²) must swap between (u+vi)⁵ and (u-vi)⁵, without systematically analyzing all four possible units in Z[i] to eliminate other configurations.

The claim that 'symmetry alone forces x=y=z at any stationary point' is unsupported; symmetric functions with symmetric constraints can have non-symmetric critical points, and the proof provides no computation to verify this assertion via Lagrange multipliers.
none
The proof falsely claims that 4·7^b - 1 has only prime divisor 3, but for b≥2 this number has other prime divisors (e.g., b=2 gives 195=3·5·13 with primes 5 and 13).
The proof claims φ acts as a 3-cycle (Q↦T↦S↦Q) on points Q, S, T, but φ is an involution (composition of two commuting involutions), which cannot have 3-cycles since φ² must equal identity.
Proof only establishes the k=2 case and explicitly admits inability to prove the general k≥3 case, which is required by the problem statement.

Circular reasoning: the proof claims S_{ij}=A_i∪B_j from |A_i∪B_j|≤i+j=|S_{ij}|, but this only shows A_i∪B_j could be a proper subset; equality requires |A_i∪B_j|=i+j which requires A_i∩B_j=∅, yet the proof derives disjointness from the equality it hasn't established.
The proof incorrectly claims the rotation angle of σₖ is 2∠Aₖ when the derivation shows it should be −∠Aₖ (or π − ∠Aₖ), with no valid geometric justification for the doubling.

The claimed inequality D(3p) ≤ 3·D(p) is false because 27p² ≤ 9p² is invalid for all positive p, and the proof incorrectly equates 9[p²+p(q+s)+(q²+qs+s²)] with 3·D(p) when the coefficient of (q²+qs+s²) doesn't match.
